meta.title: Xtracsys App Audit Wiki
meta.subtitle: User guide, audit workflows, and source reference
meta.description: Offline user guide and project reference for Xtracsys App Audit. The wiki documents practical audit workflows, evidence limits, and the source package boundary.

sections.heading: About Xtracsys App Audit
sections.body: Xtracsys App Audit is a native, read-only macOS application inventory and evidence review tool. Use the User Guide tab to run a scan, review evidence, save or compare audits, export results, and understand optional network and scheduled-audit features. Use File System for a folder-by-folder map of the project source.

sections.heading: Start using the guide
sections.body: Open User Guide for task-based instructions and interactive diagrams. The diagrams are local files included with this wiki and open in a separate tab when you need the full-size controls.

sections.heading: Operating boundaries
sections.body:
The inventory reader does not launch installed applications or install updates. Scan warnings remain visible when folders cannot be read. Update, signing, Gatekeeper, notarization, and policy results are separate observations; missing evidence is not a clean verdict.

Audit data and settings stay on the Mac. Export redaction removes personal paths, web addresses, and selected free-text fields, while the remaining app names, identifiers, and evidence may still be sensitive.

sections.heading: Use App Audit from start to finish
sections.body: This guide follows the work most people do: scan app bundles, narrow the inventory, review evidence, choose an export, and save a baseline if they need to compare changes later. App Audit reads installed apps without launching them, installing updates, or uploading the inventory.

items.title: Open App Audit
items.detail: Launch `dist/App Audit.app`. The included build requires macOS 14.4 or later and is Apple Silicon; it is ad-hoc signed and not notarized.

items.title: Start a scan
items.detail: Select Rescan. The default scope is the accessible filesystem, including mounted volumes, hidden folders, and nested helper `.app` bundles. The device filesystem `/dev` is excluded.

items.title: Review scan coverage
items.detail: Open Folders to see the selected roots and any coverage gaps. Choose a narrower folder set when that fits your task, or restore the full filesystem scope. Read warnings before treating an app as absent.

items.title: Wait for the inventory
items.detail: The app lists `.app` bundles it can read. It does not claim to inventory standalone command-line tools, scripts, services, or apps inside archives.

sections.heading: Choose the right action
rows: Export CSV or Export JSON; both use the rows currently visible after search and filters.
Keep the complete audit for later
Snapshots → Save full audit snapshot…; this preserves the full scan and collected evidence, regardless of table filters.
Compare a later scan with a baseline
Open snapshot as baseline…, rescan, then Review changes.

sections.heading: Audit flow
sections.title: App Audit: from scan to results
sections.note: An overview of the scan, optional checks, review, and the two different output choices.

sections.heading: Find and inspect apps
sections.body: Use search for an app name, bundle ID, version, or path. Filter for updates, unknown last use, or apps needing security review. Select a column heading to sort; Columns controls date, security, and location groups. Select a row for details. Reveal in Finder selects the app bundle without launching it.

sections.heading: Understand the two network switches
sections.body:
Online and trust checks controls new update-catalog checks, signing and Gatekeeper checks that may use Apple trust services, and in-app browser links. When Off, those checks are skipped while local inventory, hashes, policy review, and exports remain available. A request already in progress may finish; this app switch is not a system firewall. The setting persists between launches.

Find network devices is a separate opt-in. When On and the app is active, App Audit browses supported Bonjour service types on the local network. macOS requests Local Network permission the first time. It shows service advertisements, not a complete device inventory; quiet devices and devices without those services may not appear. Turning it Off or leaving the active app scene clears its in-memory results. App Audit does not probe network addresses or inspect remote apps.

sections.heading: Network controls
sections.title: App Audit: independent network controls
sections.note: The online/trust checks and local Bonjour discovery switches control different activities and have separate results.

items.title: Choose what to inspect
items.detail: Inspect security checks the visible app rows; the app detail panel can inspect one selected app. These checks are optional and are unavailable while Online and trust checks is Off.

items.title: Read each result with its date
items.detail: Signature, publisher, Gatekeeper, notarization, receipt, and integrity-hash results are separate observations. Old evidence can be marked stale after app files change.

items.title: Use findings as review prompts
items.detail: Findings group Action needed, Review, and Unknown with suggested next steps. A finding is evidence to investigate, not a malware or vulnerability verdict.

items.title: Keep boundaries in mind
items.detail: A valid signature does not prove an app is harmless. Collected hashes cover the main executable, Info.plist, and CodeResources, not every file in a bundle.

sections.heading: Export the view or save the full audit

items.title: Shape the current view
items.detail: Search and filter the table until it contains the rows you want to export. Export CSV and Export JSON use those currently visible rows and their available evidence.

items.title: Choose a list export
items.detail: Select Export CSV or Export JSON beside the scan actions. The JSON list has its own format; it is not a full audit snapshot.

items.title: Choose the complete record when needed
items.detail: Use Snapshots → Save full audit snapshot… to save all inventoried apps, roots and warnings, plus collected update, security, receipt, integrity, policy, and finding evidence. Table filters do not reduce it.

items.title: Review before sharing
items.detail: Audit tools → Redact personal paths & web addresses in exports applies to explicit exports for the session. Redaction does not hide app names, bundle IDs, versions, signing evidence, or all diagnostic text; inspect each exported file before posting it.

sections.heading: Keep your audit private
sections.body: Audits and settings are stored locally. Full snapshots contain local paths and installed-app inventory. Redacted exports are not guaranteed anonymization. Imported snapshots are not authenticated, so treat them as records to review rather than trusted proof.

sections.heading: Save and compare
sections.title: App Audit: save a baseline and compare
sections.note: A full snapshot keeps an earlier audit available as a baseline for a later scan.

items.title: Save a baseline
items.detail: After scanning and collecting any desired checks, choose Snapshots → Save full audit snapshot….

items.title: Open that baseline later
items.detail: Choose Open snapshot as baseline… and select the earlier snapshot. You can also use the current scan as a temporary in-memory baseline before making changes.

items.title: Run the current scan
items.detail: Rescan the current Mac using the intended scope. Different scan folders or incomplete scans can make apparent additions and removals ambiguous.

items.title: Review the comparison
items.detail: Choose Review changes to see Added, Removed, Updated, Relocated, Relocated & updated, and Replaced records. Matching uses exact paths first, then unique bundle IDs; duplicate identities are not guessed.

items.title: Treat saved evidence as historical
items.detail: The Saved audit evidence tab displays the observations captured at that time; reopening them does not run new checks.

sections.heading: Findings, policy, and exceptions
sections.body: Use Findings to review coverage gaps, verification failures, confirmed updates, integrity or signing changes, and policy exceptions. Approved-app policy is off by default and reports differences; it does not block execution or uninstall apps. If you record an exception for a finding, it applies to that evidence. Changed evidence, expiry, or revocation requires review again.

sections.heading: Scheduled audits
sections.title: App Audit: scheduled audit lifecycle
sections.note: Daily runs are optional, remain local, and use a quiet first run to establish their baseline.

sections.heading: Set up a scheduled audit (optional)
sections.body:
Open Audit tools → Scheduled audits & alerts. Configure the daily local time, update-source checks, security inspection, and notifications. The schedule is off until Enable daily audits installs App Audit’s own user LaunchAgent. Run audit now works without installing a schedule; Disable schedule removes it.

Scheduled runs can run with the window closed while the Mac user is logged in. Keep the app at its installed location and the external drive available. The first run creates a quiet baseline; later runs notify about newly observed apps, comparable changes, verified updates, and new actionable findings. Up to 30 local audits are retained. The global Online and trust checks setting still applies.

sections.heading: A few common questions
rows: Review Folders and scan warnings. The selected roots may not include it, or the app bundle may be unreadable.
Confirm Find network devices is On, the app is active, and macOS Local Network permission is allowed. Discovery only sees supported Bonjour advertisements.
Update or trust checks are unavailable
Turn Online and trust checks On. Cached results keep their original dates and are not new checks.
A removed app appears in comparison
Check whether the two audits used different folders or either scan had warnings. Missing coverage is not proof that the app was removed.
I need to share a record
Use a filtered CSV/JSON list for visible rows, or a full snapshot for all collected audit evidence. Enable redaction if appropriate, then review the exported file.
